title: FFLLW cannot be sharpened to chi <= girth

problemStatement.formal: Show that the classical FFLLW condition cannot be strengthened from chi(G) < girth(G) to chi(G) <= girth(G); the K3 girth-3 witness has chi = girth and no classically robust orientation.
problemStatement.plain: Can the FFLLW sufficient condition chi < girth be sharpened to chi <= girth? No: K3 is the boundary counterexample in the classical formulation.
whyMatters: This separates the sharp classical FFLLW threshold from the rank-based formulation used elsewhere in the Erdos1006 family.

proven: `k3_no_classical_robust` proves K3 has no classically robust orientation.
`girth3_classical_witness` packages K3 as the girth-3, chromatic-number-3 witness in Erdos1006OQ02.lean.
open: The broader classical FFLLW lower bound is still carried by the `ffllw_classical` axiom.

insights: K3 has chi = girth = 3 and no classically robust orientation, so chi <= girth is not a sufficient replacement for chi < girth.
Rank-based robust orientation is intentionally distinguished from the classical path-based definition in Erdos1006OQ02.lean.
